event_name: Gilles de Rais tried for heresy and demonology
significance: Gilles de Rais, Marshal of France and former companion-in-arms of Joan of Arc, was tried by ecclesiastical and ducal courts on charges of heresy, sodomy, and invocation of demons; the case illustrates the extension of witchcraft-adjacent charges to elite male figures with political vulnerability and the overlap between demonological prosecution and factional power struggles.
source_method: Trial records in Georges Bataille, Le Procès de Gilles de Rais (1959); analyzed in Ankarloo and Clark, Witchcraft and Magic in Europe: The Middle Ages (2002)
